planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring into well-drained, neutral to alkaline soil, siting it where it gets some open light; avoid disturbing the root ball, since this species resents transplanting even more than its wetland-loving relatives.

directions: Ozark leatherwood was only recently recognized as distinct from the more familiar Dirca palustris, and it is endemic to limestone and dolomite glades, bluffs, and open rocky woodlands of the Ozark Plateau in Missouri, Arkansas, and Oklahoma. Unlike its wetland-associated relatives, it tolerates drier, well-drained, calcareous soils and tends to grow as a larger, more upright multi-stemmed shrub with broader elliptic leaves. Tiny pale-yellow, tubular flowers open on bare, pliable stems in late winter well before the foliage emerges, followed by small green berry-like fruits in late spring. Because nursery stock is still scarce, buy only from native-plant specialists propagating from seed or cuttings, and give plants a lightly shaded to sun-dappled site with excellent drainage rather than the constantly moist ground preferred by other Dirca species.
